description:
Add a release policy to an organization, or replace the one with the same name. A policy runs its checker on every publish. It monitors by default: it records findings and never refuses a release. enforcement "block" with block_at refuses a release that has a finding at or above that severity, or that the checker could not evaluate. list_policies shows the checkers and their settings.

Replacing a policy replaces its settings: pass every non-secret setting again. A change to a policy applies to releases not yet decided. Changing a policy's enforcement or settings never changes a decided evaluation, and a running policy evaluation keeps the checker and enforcement it started with. A running policy evaluation whose checker hasn't started yet uses the current settings. Removing a policy, or changing its checker, cancels its running policy evaluations, so releases that waited only on it go ahead.

A checker with secret fields, such as an API token, does not take them here. The answer carries a request whose url an Admin opens, signed in to Valet, to enter them; the policy is saved when they do, and a field left blank keeps its stored value. A request is made only when a required secret is not stored yet, or replace_secrets is true to enter them again. Say in reason why the checker needs them. Give the person the url, then follow the request with get_request. Never ask for a secret in this conversation. Otherwise the policy saves at once. Requires connecting a Valet account. Requires the Admin role.

block_at.description: The lowest severity that blocks. Required with enforcement block.

checker.description: Required. The checker to run, spelled as list_policies reports it, such as catalog:secrets.

enforcement.description: monitor (the default) records findings and never refuses a release. block refuses one with a finding at or above block_at.

org_name.description: The Valet organization that owns the policy. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

policy.description: Required. The policy's name: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, such as dependencies. An existing name is replaced.

reason.description: Required when the checker has secret fields that are not stored yet. One plain sentence, shown to the person on the request page, saying why the value is needed, such as: The app charges cards and needs your Stripe key. At most 280 characters.

replace_secrets.description: Ask the person to enter the checker's secrets again, replacing the stored ones. The request lists every secret field, required or not.

settings.description: The checker's non-secret settings, as field name to value. Secret fields are entered by a person on the request page, never here.

name: set_policy
title: Add or replace a release policy
